question.text: What will the IEA's November 2026 Oil Market Report say about the change in world oil demand in 2026 (y/y, mb/d)?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the 2026 year-on-year change in world oil demand as reported in the IEA's [Oil Market Report – November 2026](https://www.iea.org/reports/oil-market-report-november-2026), scheduled for publication at 10:00 Paris time on 13 November 2026. The governing figure is the full-year 2026 annual-average y/y change stated in that report's demand overview/highlights, which the OMR gives in million barrels per day to one decimal place — for example, if it states that world oil demand falls by 2.7 mb/d on average in 2026, the question resolves as -2.7, and a stated rise of 0.4 mb/d resolves as 0.4. If the overview states the figure only in thousands of barrels per day, it is converted by dividing by 1,000 (e.g. -2,650 kb/d resolves as -2.65). The figure as first published in the November 2026 edition governs; later revisions (for example in the December 2026 OMR or in IEA databases) do not affect resolution, and if publication is delayed beyond 13 November 2026 the question resolves once that edition is published.
question.fine_print: The figure refers to the IEA's own global oil demand series for total liquids for calendar year 2026 as a whole (full-year annual average), not to a quarterly figure and not to another institution's estimate. If the IEA's November 2026 report page is unavailable or the figure cannot be read from it, [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) reporting the figure from the IEA's November 2026 OMR will be used.

research:
I could not open the IEA's November or October report pages (the IEA site returned a 403 error), and the November edition does not come out until 13 November 2026, so nothing settles the question yet. The latest figure is October's: 2026 world oil demand down 2.6 mb/d. Several outlets report that number, and a search snippet quotes the IEA's own page saying the same.

### 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-03: The [November 2026 OMR](https://www.iea.org/reports/oil-market-report-november-2026) is not published. It is due 13 Nov, 10:00 Paris time.
- 2026-10-14: The [October OMR](https://www.iea.org/reports/oil-market-report-october-2026) put 2026 demand at 102.4 mb/d, down 2.6 mb/d y/y, with 4Q26 down 2.5 mb/d. A search snippet quoting the IEA page reads: "fall by 2.5 mb/d y-o-y in 4Q26 and 2.6 mb/d on average in 2026." One snippet dates the IEA page "10 October"; secondary sources say 14 October. Diesel is about 25% of the decline. [forextradingcommunity](https://forextradingcommunity.com/news/iea-oil-market-report-october-2026/), [globaltradingoutlook](https://www.globaltradingoutlook.com/markets/iea-october-oil-market-report-demand-diesel-stock-releases/)
- October quarterly y/y figures: 2Q26 -5.0, 3Q26 -3.7, 4Q26 -2.5 mb/d. The IEA left its rest-of-year projections "largely unchanged because of renewed attacks in the region in October." Hormuz oil flows rose 3.7 mb/d to 10.9 mb/d in September. [globaltradingoutlook](https://www.globaltradingoutlook.com/markets/iea-october-oil-market-report-demand-diesel-stock-releases/)

### 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question. Note a timing point: if the 2Q and 3Q estimates hold, the full-year figure depends mostly on revised 3Q data and on the 4Q assumption.

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-02/03: Iran offered to reopen Hormuz within two days if the US lifts its blockade, eases sanctions and halts fighting. Qatar is mediating. Trump says he is "in no rush." The strait is still closed, and a tanker hit a mine on 2 Nov. Brent fell 7.6% to $104.77 after closing at $117.64 on 30 Oct. [Seoul Economic Daily](https://en.sedaily.com/international/2026/11/03/iran-offers-to-reopen-hormuz-in-two-days-oil-plunges-7)
- 2026-11-01: The G7 began releasing 100 mb of strategic oil and diesel reserves over four months. 11 EU countries are adding 42.6 mb, with IEA support. [infobae](https://www.infobae.com/america/agencias/2026/11/01/empiezan-a-salir-al-mercado-los-100-millones-de-barriles-de-petroleo-prometidos-por-el-g7/)
- 2026-11-01: OPEC+ (seven core members) kept December targets unchanged. [Epoch Times](https://www.theepochtimes.com/world/opec-holds-december-crude-oil-output-targets-steady-6112062)
- 2026-11-02: The World Bank expects energy prices to rise 32% in 2026. [ce.cn](http://www.ce.cn/xwzx/gnsz/gdxw/202611/t20261103_3280891.shtml)
- Oct 2026: Attacks on ships hit wartime highs. The IMO counted 34 attacks between 28 Sep and 27 Oct. Hormuz transits fell to a two-month low in early October, with crude crossings down 27%. Kpler put flows at 11.6 mb/d in the week to 13 Oct, about 68% of the pre-war level. [The National](https://www.thenationalnews.com/business/2026/10/08/hormuz-traffic-hits-lowest-level-in-two-months-as-tanker-attacks-surge/), [Lloyd's List](https://www.lloydslistintelligence.com/resources/blog/strait-of-hormuz-brief-22-october-2026), [Maritime Executive](https://maritime-executive.com/index.php/article/hormuz-transits-fall-to-lowest-level-in-two-months-as-attacks-increase)
- Oct 2026: OIES says Dated Brent averaged $126/bbl over 1-23 Oct, compared with $116.89 in September. [OIES](https://www.oxfordenergy.org/wpcms/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/OIES-Oil-Monthly-Issue-58.pdf)

### 4. Base rates and revision path
- IEA 2026 growth estimates: May -0.42; June -1.1; July -1.0; Aug -1.6; Sep -2.5; Oct -2.6 mb/d. [IEA May PDF](https://iea.blob.core.windows.net/assets/2b89a47b-34a2-40e0-90ff-68f7ccd80715/-13MAY2026__OilMarketReport_publicversion.pdf), [CNBC Aug](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/12/iea-oil-demand-hormuz.html)
- Month-to-month changes: -0.7, +0.1, -0.6, -0.9, -0.1. Five of six editions revised the figure down. The latest change was small (-0.1).
- Sources conflict on the August-to-September step. One says September was "around 940 kb/d more" than August. The question background ties 941 kb/d to the July-to-August step instead. [Argus](https://www.argusmedia.com/pt/news-and-insights/latest-market-news/2826224-iea-sees-big-oil-demand-fall-but-still-2026-deficit)
- From September to October, the quarterly figures moved: 2Q improved by 0.3 mb/d (-5.3 to -5.0), 3Q worsened by 0.3 (-3.4 to -3.7) and 4Q worsened by 0.5 (-2.0 to -2.5). [streamlinefeed](https://streamlinefeed.co.ke/news/iea-deepens-2026-oil-demand-cut-as-war-squeezes-supply)
- As a rough guide, one month of the year (about 1/12) moving by 1 mb/d shifts the annual average by about 0.08 mb/d. Moving the whole of 4Q by 1 mb/d shifts it by about 0.25.

### 5. Other forecasts
- EIA October STEO: 2026 world demand 102.4 mb/d, previously 102.6. This comes from a Newsquawk headline I could not check against the EIA site. The question background reports the EIA's change as -2.0 mb/d y/y. [Newsquawk](https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/us-eia-steo-2026-world-oil-demand-1024mln-bpd-preev-1026mln-bpd-2027-1046mln-bpd-prev-105mln-bpd)
- OPEC October MOMR: +0.2 mb/d growth in 2026. [Enerdata](https://www.enerdata.net/publications/daily-energy-news/opec-sees-global-oil-demand-growth-02-mbd-2026-rebounding-2027.html)
- Prediction markets: I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on the IEA figure. The Kalshi markets supplied with the question (US output, GDP, exports and others) do not match it.

### 6. Upcoming events before 13 Nov
- 2026-11-03: US midterm elections. Trump said "No" when asked whether he would resume strikes afterwards. [Seoul Economic Daily](https://en.sedaily.com/international/2026/11/03/iran-offers-to-reopen-hormuz-in-two-days-oil-plunges-7)
- Early November: the Qatar-mediated talks on Iran's two-day reopening offer. China plans to send an envoy to Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia in early to mid November. [CBS](https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-strait-of-hormuz-sanctions/)
- About 10 Nov: the EIA's November STEO. About 11-12 Nov: OPEC's November MOMR. I did not confirm either date.
- The November OMR will add September and October demand data. Two things pull in opposite directions. Brent was higher in October (about $126) and attacks increased, which points to more demand loss. A possible Hormuz deal, plus the oil price drop on 2 Nov and the stock releases, could ease 4Q prices. With only about seven weeks of the year left after publication, any deal would do little to the annual average.

Sources: IEA pages linked above; [oilmonster](https://www.oilmonster.com/article/iea-cuts-oil-demand-again-as-2026-use-falls-26m-bpd/8695); [vantagemarkets](https://www.vantagemarkets.com/market-news/oil-price-today-iea-brent-october-15-2026/); [OGJ](https://www.ogj.com/general-interest/economics-markets/news/55397558/iea-revises-down-2026-oil-demand-forecast).

# IEA November 2026 OMR: 2026 world oil demand change (research notes)

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-03: The IEA's November 2026 OMR page is not published yet. It is due 2026-11-13 at 10:00 Paris time. When I tried to fetch the October report page directly, it returned HTTP 403, so I relied on secondary coverage. [IEA Oct OMR](https://www.iea.org/reports/oil-market-report-october-2026)
- 2026-10-14: Latest value, from the October OMR: 2026 demand falls 2.6 mb/d to 102.4 mb/d. The year-on-year falls by quarter are 5.0 mb/d in 2Q, 3.7 mb/d in 3Q and 2.5 mb/d forecast for 4Q. Diesel accounts for about 25% of the loss. [globaltradingoutlook](https://www.globaltradingoutlook.com/markets/iea-october-oil-market-report-demand-diesel-stock-releases/); [forextradingcommunity](https://forextradingcommunity.com/news/iea-oil-market-report-october-2026/)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. Because 2Q and 3Q are largely history, a change to the annual number would have to come from revised history for Jul-Sep or from a revised 4Q path. As a rough guide, each 0.4 mb/d change in 4Q moves the annual figure by about 0.1 mb/d.
- 2026-10-14: The October OMR assumed hostilities would ease gradually and product availability would improve. It left the rest-of-year Hormuz flow projections "largely unchanged because of renewed attacks in October." [oilmonster](https://www.oilmonster.com/article/iea-cuts-oil-demand-again-as-2026-use-falls-26m-bpd/8695); [globaltradingoutlook](https://www.globaltradingoutlook.com/markets/iea-october-oil-market-report-demand-diesel-stock-releases/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-03: Brent was around $105 after a US "defensive" strike on Iran's Qeshm Island. Mediators led by Qatar are working on a framework where Iran stops attacks in Hormuz and the US lifts its port blockade. No deal yet. [newsbytes](https://www.newsbytesapp.com/news/business/us-strike-at-qeshm-island-lifts-brent-to-10525/tldr); [CBS live](https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-negotiations-midterms/)
- 2026-11-02: Brent fell about 6-7% (one report gives $106.54) on hopes for a settlement. Iran said it could reopen Hormuz within two days if its conditions are met. UKMTO puts Hormuz traffic about 70% below pre-war levels. [goodreturns](https://www.goodreturns.in/lw/wealth/markets/crude-oil-price-today-brent-wti-rebound-7-percent-fall-us-iran-strike-1544819.html)
- 2026-11-02: The World Bank expects energy prices to rise 32% in 2026, according to an article from ce.cn. [ce.cn](http://www.ce.cn/xwzx/gnsz/gdxw/202611/t20261103_3280891.shtml)
- 2026-11-01: OPEC+ (seven core members) kept December targets unchanged. Reuters, as cited by Al-Masry Al-Youm, had Brent December closing at $117.64. The G7 began releasing 100 mb of crude and diesel reserves over four months, plus 42.6 mb from 11 EU countries. [Epoch Times](https://www.theepochtimes.com/world/opec-holds-december-crude-oil-output-targets-steady-6112062); [infobae](https://www.infobae.com/america/agencias/2026/11/01/empiezan-a-salir-al-mercado-los-100-millones-de-barriles-de-petroleo-prometidos-por-el-g7/)
- 2026-10-25 to 11-01: Iran's IRGC/IRIB say at least 11 tankers have been hit or set on fire since 25 October, some by mines. The US disputes this. Oman rescued 25 crew from a burning tanker on 30 October. A tracker shows Hormuz "closed, day 247." [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/30/oman-rescues-25-from-burning-oil-tanker-in-strait-of-hormuz); [oilprice](https://oilprice.com/Latest-Energy-News/World-News/Oil-Jumps-2-as-Iran-Steps-Up-Attacks-on-Hormuz-Tankers.html); [straits.live](https://straits.live/)
- Around mid-October, as reported in the October OMR: Dated Brent was about $134/bbl when the report was written. Diesel peaked above $200/bbl in September and remains nearly double the crude price. [globaltradingoutlook](https://www.globaltradingoutlook.com/markets/iea-october-oil-market-report-demand-diesel-stock-releases/)

## 4. Base rates and revision history
- 2026 path of the IEA's 2026 growth figure: January +0.93, May -0.42, June -1.1, July -1.0, August -1.6, September -2.5, October -2.6 (mb/d). [OGJ](https://www.ogj.com/general-interest/economics-markets/news/55397558/iea-revises-down-2026-oil-demand-forecast); [CNBC Aug](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/12/iea-oil-demand-hormuz.html); [May OMR PDF](https://iea.blob.core.windows.net/assets/2b89a47b-34a2-40e0-90ff-68f7ccd80715/-13MAY2026__OilMarketReport_publicversion.pdf)
- Month-to-month changes since June: +0.1, -0.6, -0.9, -0.1. The background says August was 941 kb/d steeper than July, which does not match the rounded -1.0 to -1.6 move. The July figure may have been about -0.66 unrounded, but I could not verify this. Six of the last seven editions were downgrades, and the most recent one was small (about -0.1).
- In the October edition the IEA also cut the 2027 rebound from 2.6 mb/d to 2.0 mb/d, which signals a more pessimistic outlook overall. [oilmonster](https://www.oilmonster.com/article/iea-cuts-oil-demand-again-as-2026-use-falls-26m-bpd/8695)
- In normal years revisions run about 0.1-0.3 mb/d per month. Late in the year the annual figure usually moves less, because most of the year is already history.

## 5. Other forecasts
- October 2026, from the IEF comparison: OPEC put 2026 at +0.2 mb/d (105.7 mb/d), EIA at -2.0 mb/d (102.4 mb/d) and IEA at -2.6 mb/d. [IEF PDF](https://www.ief.org/_resources/files/news/comparative-analysis-of-monthly-reports-on-the-oil-market/october-2026/ief-comparative-analysis-10-2026.pdf)
- A MarketScreener/Dow Jones piece of uncertain date cites an EIA 2026 decline of 1.1 mb/d to 102.9 mb/d. This is probably an older STEO. [marketscreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/eia-sees-lower-oil-demand-as-middle-east-conflict-drags-on-ce7f5cdada8cf72d)
- Prediction markets: I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on IEA demand figures. None of the Kalshi markets supplied with the question match it; they cover US output, GDP, exports and similar. Kalshi prices US 2026 GDP growth of 2.1-2.5% at 0.78, which suggests markets do not expect a sharp US recession.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution (13 Nov)
- 2026-11-10: The EIA's November STEO, which will show its world consumption revision. [EIA STEO](https://www.eia.gov/outlooks/steo)
- Around 11-12 November: OPEC's November MOMR. I did not verify the exact date.
- Ongoing: US-Iran talks mediated by Qatar over a Hormuz-for-blockade deal. Any deal or escalation before the IEA's data cutoff, likely a few days before 13 November, could change the 4Q and 2027 assumptions.
- Ongoing: The G7/IEA stock release that began 1 November, including diesel, could ease product shortages. Late-October tanker attacks and Brent at $105-118 point the other way.
- New monthly data from the OECD and from China, India and other Asian countries for August-September will feed into revisions of 3Q history.

forecasts.reasoning:
**(a) Time left:** About 10 days. The November OMR is due on 13 November 2026.

**(b) Latest known value:** The October 2026 OMR, published 14 October 2026, put 2026 world oil demand at -2.6 mb/d y/y (102.4 mb/d). Its quarterly figures were 2Q -5.0, 3Q -3.7 and 4Q -2.5 mb/d.

**(c) If nothing changed:** -2.6 mb/d.

**(d) If the trend continued:** About -2.7 to -2.8 mb/d. Five of the last six editions revised the figure down, though October's step was only -0.1. October conditions point to a further modest cut:
- Brent averaged about $126 in October, against about $117 in September.
- Attacks on ships hit wartime highs.
- Hormuz flows fell back.

On the other side, early-November developments could make the IEA hold 4Q roughly steady: the Iran reopening offer, Brent falling to about $105, and the release of strategic stocks. With 2Q and 3Q largely data-based, a 1 mb/d change across all of 4Q moves the annual figure by only about 0.25 mb/d.

**(e) Historical variation:** Revisions are normally 0.1 to 0.3 mb/d per edition. In 2026 they have run from -0.9 to +0.1 per month. Revisions to the 2025 baseline can also shift the growth figure.

**(f) Expert and market expectations:**
- The EIA is at -2.0 and OPEC at +0.2 mb/d. Neither is likely to pull the IEA, which has kept its own downgrade path.
- There is no prediction market on this figure.

**(g) Surprise scenarios:**
- **Low:** Weak September and October data, such as large non-OECD diesel and jet losses, combined with a deeper macro downgrade, cut 3Q and 4Q by around 1 mb/d each, giving about -3.2 to -3.5.
- **High:** A Hormuz deal is signed before publication, prices fall sharply, and the September data come in better than estimated. Together with an upward revision to 2Q, that could lift the figure to about -2.1 to -2.2.

(d) If the trend continued, the answer would be about -2.7 to -2.8. Five of the last six editions revised demand down. The latest step was small (-0.1). In October, the 3Q and 4Q estimates were cut while 2Q was revised up.

(e) Historical variation: month-to-month revisions in 2026 have been -0.7, +0.1, -0.6, -0.9 and -0.1. With most of the year now observed, a 1 mb/d shift across all of 4Q moves the annual figure by only about 0.25. A single month of new data moves it by about 0.08. (f) Experts and markets:
- Pointing to more demand loss: Dated Brent averaged about $126 in October, up from $117 in September. Tanker attacks hit wartime highs and Hormuz transits fell.
- Pointing the other way: Iran's reopening offer, the oil price drop on 2 November and the G7/IEA stock releases. These matter mostly for 4Q assumptions and could temper downgrades.
- Other forecasters: the EIA has -2.0 and OPEC +0.2. Both are less bearish than the IEA but do not anchor it.
- I found no prediction market on this figure.

(g) Unexpected scenarios:
- Low outcome: September and October data reveal severe demand destruction, with diesel rationing and recessionary collapse in Asia. The IEA cuts 3Q by a further 0.5 and 4Q by 1 mb/d, taking the year to about -3.2 or lower.
- High outcome: a Hormuz reopening deal is struck before publication, and stronger-than-assumed 3Q data come in. Alternatively, a 2025 baseline revision lifts the growth figure. The IEA could then revise up to about -2.3 or -2.2.

My distribution is centred on -2.7, with a modest downward skew because recent conditions point to further cuts. I have kept the tails wide given how large revisions have been this year.
